message:
Aero-Rotor Lead:

I confirm what Safety-Control Integrator takes from the Braking ideas for wind turbines (E42) that almost all rotor brakes are spring-applied fail-safe, which from my side means the blades must keep storm driving torque below the pad so the spring can park it. Plain words: stalled blades spill lift like a flagged sail so the stopped rotor only shivers instead of driving. The dynamic pressure (E71) is 296 Pa at 22 m/s, the running torques (E73) are 0.0218 N·m at 5 m/s and 0.105 N·m at 11 m/s from the shaft powers (E11) 3.27 W and (E12) 34.7 W, and my stalled-blade estimate with lift collapsed to drag gives about 0.25 N·m parked driving torque, below the 0.400 N·m pad in the spring disc (C21) and well below the upsized 0.800 N·m hold in the upgraded stop (E70), like a hand grip beating a shopping-bag pull.

Start and tip speed fit low-wind production without noise penalty, for Power-Systems Engineer. Plain words: the rotor still pulls away at light wind and the tips stay well below aircraft speeds. Tip speed at 11 m/s with Tip-Speed Ratio (TSR), meaning tip speed divided by wind speed, 6 is 66.0 m/s in the tip check (E72), about highway-car speed and Mach 0.19 so no transonic noise, while starting torque 0.0218 N·m in the operating torques (E73) exceeds typical outrunner cogging of order 0.01 N·m so the 1.43e+03 Revolutions Per Minute (RPM), meaning shaft turns per minute, low-wind speed (E14) is reachable.

For the Manager on the weakest sense function I add a distant-field second means in the centrifugal trip (C28) by steam-governor analogy. Plain words: like a steam-engine governor whose balls fling out with speed, two small hub weights fling out above about 3.30e+03 RPM to open the trip loop with no power needed. That maps centrifugal force proportional to speed squared to overspeed detection, backing the latched trip (C20) at the 315 RPM trip target from 10 percent of the top speed (E13) 3.15e+03 RPM, and stays inside the 40 cm rotor in the side-view layout (E50).

Not ready, because power-curve and parked-torque bench tests still need Manager decision.
